questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Release the brake until the tire grips again, then brake again.
Release the brake and use only the front brake.
Keep the brake locked until the motorcycle stops.
Release the brake and coast to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the brake locked until the motorcycle stops.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while braking, keep the brake locked. Do not release it. Hold it locked until the motorcycle comes to a complete stop.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a cause of motorcycle wobbling?

options.text: Incorrect tire pressure
Improper loading
Unsuitable accessories
Uneven road

questions.correctAnswerText: Uneven road
questions.explanation: Wobbles usually come from improper loading, unsuitable accessories, or incorrect tire pressure. Do not speed up to escape a wobble.

questions.question: In New Hampshire, at what blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is a person age 21 or older legally intoxicated?

options.text: 0.02 percent
0.04 percent
0.06 percent
0.08 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: A person of legal drinking age with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated. It is illegal and dangerous to ride a motorcycle while intoxicated.

questions.question: Which part of a lane should you always avoid?

options.text: The left portion
The center portion
The right portion
No part should always be avoided.

questions.correctAnswerText: No part should always be avoided.
questions.explanation: There is no lane position that is always best or always worst. Choose your lane position based on current riding conditions.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a benefit of riding in a tight group?

options.text: It uses less road space.
The group is easy to see.
The group is less likely to get split up.
Riders reach their destination faster in a tight group than in a spread-out group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders reach their destination faster in a tight group than in a spread-out group.
questions.explanation: Riding in a tight group is better than riding spread out because it uses less road space, is easier to see, and is less likely to get separated at traffic lights and during passes. However, group speed does not change based on how close riders are to each other.

questions.question: When crossing angled railroad tracks, how should you approach them?

options.text: Go straight ahead in your lane.
Approach at a 45-degree angle.
Approach at a 90-degree angle.
Go fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go straight ahead in your lane.
questions.explanation: The safest way to cross angled railroad tracks is to go straight in your lane. Turning to hit the tracks at a right angle is dangerous because it may push you into another lane.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, which instruction should you NOT give them?

options.text: Get on after the engine starts.
Sit as far forward as you can without crowding me.
Hold firmly onto my waist, hips, or belt.
Feel free to talk whenever you want.

questions.correctAnswerText: Feel free to talk whenever you want.
questions.explanation: Passengers should not talk or move around unnecessarily so you can focus on riding. Passengers should board only after the engine starts. They should sit forward without crowding you and hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Slow or stop
Left turn
Right turn
Backing up

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow or stop
questions.explanation: Riders can use hand signals instead of or along with turn signals. When the left arm is bent at the elbow and points downward, it means the rider plans to slow down or stop.

questions.question: If a friend has been drinking and wants to drive, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Ask other friends to talk them out of driving.
Arrange other transportation for them.
Tell them to take less-crowded roads.
Slow down their drinking pace.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell them to take less-crowded roads.
questions.explanation: You can stop someone from driving while intoxicated by arranging other transportation, keeping them busy to slow their drinking, stopping them from leaving before they are sober, and getting other friends to help. Do not suggest they take less-crowded roads instead—they should not drive at all.

questions.question: How can a motorcyclist stop other vehicles from sharing their lane?

options.text: Ride on the left side of the lane.
Ride in the center of the lane.
Give dirty looks to drivers who try to share.
Ride in a zigzag pattern to fill the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when another driver might try to squeeze in next to you. This discourages them from attempting to share your lane.

questions.question: When do you NOT need to increase your following distance?

options.text: When the road is slippery
When there is heavy traffic
When you can see through the vehicle in front of you
When it is raining

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see through the vehicle in front of you
questions.explanation: You need more following distance if your motorcycle takes longer to stop. Increase your distance if the road is slippery, you cannot see through the vehicle ahead, or traffic is heavy and another vehicle might pull in front of you.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group?

options.text: Just behind the leader
In front of the group
At the back of the group
Next to the leader

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This allows experienced riders behind them to watch and help if needed.

questions.question: What is the best thing to do when it is raining?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane
Pull off the road until the rain stops
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars
Increase your speed

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars
questions.explanation: Wet roads are most slippery at the start of rain when oil has not yet washed away. The safest choice is to ride in the tire tracks left by cars. The left track is often the best choice.

questions.question: Where should you ride to best handle a wind blast from a passing vehicle?

options.text: In the left portion of the lane
In the center portion of the lane
In the right portion of the lane
On the shoulder

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center portion of the lane
questions.explanation: Riding in the center of your lane gives you the most room to move if a wind blast pushes you to either side.

questions.question: What should you do when stopping behind a vehicle?

options.text: Stop far back, then slowly move closer
Stay well behind the vehicle
Stop quickly right behind the vehicle
Stay about four car lengths back

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay well behind the vehicle
questions.explanation: Stay well behind the vehicle even when both are stopped. The vehicle ahead might back up, or you may need space to move away from a vehicle coming up behind you.

questions.question: How should you brake for normal stops?

options.text: Use only the rear brake
Use only the front brake
Use both the front and rear brakes
Alternate between the front and rear brakes

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when slowing down or stopping, even for normal stops.

questions.question: Because motorcycles are hard to see at night, riders should:

options.text: Slow down when riding at night
Sound their horn many times when riding at night
Not ride at night
Stay directly in front of another vehicle to use their headlights

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down when riding at night
questions.explanation: Riding safely at night includes reducing your speed, increasing following distance, using another vehicle's lights to see ahead, using your high beam (unless following or meeting traffic), and adjusting your position in the lane.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When traffic is light
When traffic is heavy
When you can see through vehicles in front of you
When there is good and clear weather

questions.correctAnswerText: When traffic is heavy
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when conditions need longer stopping distance, such as poor weather, nighttime, when you cannot see through the vehicle ahead, or when traffic is heavy.

questions.question: Why should you ride on the left side of your lane when preparing to pass?

options.text: The right side could be slippery
It gives you a better view of hazards in the next lane
People don't expect to be passed on their left
It puts you in the car's rearview mirror

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you a better view of hazards in the next lane
questions.explanation: Riding on the left side of your lane improves your sight line and makes you more visible to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: How should you load cargo on a motorcycle?

options.text: Pack heavier items in front of the tank bag
Pack lighter items near the front
Avoid placing items over the rear axle
Place items behind the rear axle

questions.correctAnswerText: Pack heavier items in front of the tank bag
questions.explanation: Pack heavier items in front of the tank bag. Load should be over or in front of the rear axle. Placing the load behind the rear axle can affect your control.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, EXCEPT:

options.text: Help you see other drivers and be seen by them.
Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
Help you avoid road hazards.
Block your escape route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Block your escape route.
questions.explanation: A good lane position should help you see others and be seen. It should help you avoid wind, other drivers' blind spots, and road hazards. Your lane position should also keep other drivers out of your lane and give you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: When following a car, the best place to ride in the lane is:

options.text: The left portion.
The center portion.
The right portion.
The left or right portions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The center portion.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane when following a car. This position puts you in the driver's rearview mirror, where they look most often. Using the center lane position increases your chances of being seen.

questions.question: If you lock the rear tire on a dry road surface, you should:

options.text: Release and re-apply the rear brake.
Keep it locked until you completely stop.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake and use both brakes to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you completely stop.
questions.explanation: If you lock the rear brake on a dry road, you can keep it locked until you stop completely. You should still be able to steer your motorcycle with a locked rear wheel.

questions.question: The best protection for a rider is:

options.text: Space between your vehicle and other vehicles.
A good leather jacket.
Sturdy boots.
Knowledge of motorcycle laws.

questions.correctAnswerText: Space between your vehicle and other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Your best protection against crashes is to keep distance between you and other vehicles. Leave plenty of space so you have time to react if another driver makes a mistake. Wearing proper gear is also important for protection.

questions.question: Fatigue can be increased by:

options.text: Stopping frequently.
Riding in cool weather.
Being comfortable during your ride.
Starting a ride late in the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding in cool weather.
questions.explanation: Dress to protect yourself from tiring conditions like wind and rain. Ride no more than six hours per day. Stop for a break at least every two hours. Avoid using stimulants because you may become very tired when they wear off.
